deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a draft, in Gauss's hand, of a short German book notice. The format ('Göttingen. b[ey] Röwer. Title ... 32 Seiten in Octav') is that of a review for the Göttingische gelehrte Anzeigen. The book is the first edition of the pseudo-Ulpianic procedural tract 'Ulpianus de edendo', taken from Best's copy of a Harleian manuscript in the British Museum. The editors are a Georg August M[...] (name hard to read; the machine reads 'Meyerth', the image looks closer to 'Meywerth'), Dr. jur. and procurator general at the criminal court of the Harz district, and Ernst Spangenberg, Dr. jur. and assessor at the Göttingen court of first instance.

The notice tells the story of the find:
- Someone remarked that the Catalogus Codicum MSS. Angliae et Hiberniae listed unknown writings of Ulpian.
- Hofrat Gustav Hugo therefore wrote to Geheimsecretär Best in London.
- Best, with Mr. Planta (Joseph Planta of the British Museum), searched the Museum's manuscripts. They found a tract titled 'Ulpianus de edendo' and sent a third of it in copy to Hugo.
- Hugo saw that the piece was not by Ulpian but was still worth attention, because it surveys the whole Roman civil procedure. He printed a sample in his Civilistisches Magazin (vol. 1, pp. 375-82; in the Auszug pp. 135-39).

The notice then lists the chapters: Prooemium; de ingressu litium; de in jus vocando; de eremodicio; de excusationibus; de satisdationibus; de juramento calumniae; de ordine quaestionum; de compensationibus; de plurispetitione; de exceptionibus. It also mentions two small genuine Ulpian fragments taken from Boethius.

Finally it discusses authorship. The author is unknown: perhaps a later or younger 'Ulpian' or someone with a similar name. He is certainly not one of the Glossators, being apparently older than they are. He may have been French, since Paris is mentioned on p. 9, if that reading is right. The editors add parallel passages from the Corpus Juris, which show that the pseudo-Ulpian copied much verbatim.

This sheet sits in Math.13 between two mathematical pages:
- The previous page has bracket identities for an alternating 'area' form [x,x';y,y'] and a rotation by 45°.
- The next page has lattice-point and floor-function sums Σ[kB/A] for Gaussian integers, connected to biquadratic reciprocity.

Neither of those connects to the content of this page. The sheet was evidently reused as scrap or bound in by accident.

results.what: Non-mathematical draft book notice (Göttingische gelehrte Anzeigen style) of the edition 'Ulpianus de edendo' (pseudo-Ulpian tract on Roman civil procedure, from Best's copy of a Harleian MS)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics. It is a German draft review of a legal-historical edition. It is perhaps a mild curiosity that Gauss drafted or copied a jurisprudence notice for the Göttingen review journal, but it has no mathematical significance.
transcription_corrections: 'b. Röwer' = 'bey Röwer' (the Göttingen publisher Röwer), not a person's initial.
Editor's surname read as 'Meyerth' looks more like 'Meywerth' in the image; uncertain.
'Haenels[?] Bemerkung': the image looks more like 'Haimerius'/'Heinerius' (possibly Heineccius?); uncertain, and 'Haenel' is doubtful.
'de heremodicio' is the manuscript's spelling of 'de eremodicio' (default of appearance); the chapter title is correct as written.
'denn er ist vorzüglich alt dieser' is likely 'denn er ist vermuthlich älter als diese' (i.e. older than the Glossators).
'Schüler[?]' after 'jüngeren Ulpian' is uncertain; it may be another name form.
